commonPrompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset: immersive full-screen background for a scientific mission center. Generate a NEW wide 16:9 landscape photograph, 1536x864 or larger. First-person eye-level view inside a convincing contemporary molecular drug-discovery research laboratory at a university institute. Premium documentary architectural photography, extremely precise real equipment details, believable cable routing and material joints, practical scientific layout. Light grey epoxy resin benches, pale mineral walls, brushed aluminum instrument housings, glass partitions, anti-static flooring, soft neutral overhead laboratory lighting with restrained teal instrument indicators. Sophisticated, tangible, cinematic depth but clearly a REAL WORKING SCIENTIFIC LAB, never a cozy home office or decorative corporate lobby. Good midtones, crisp equipment at sides, clear negative space through center for an interface to overlay. ABSOLUTELY NO PEOPLE anywhere, no faces, portraits, silhouettes, hands, human reflections or people on screens. No legible lettering, captions, labels, logos or watermarks. Screens can show plausible abstract scientific plots and molecular structure visualization, NOT imaginary holograms or floating molecules. No coffee shop decor, wood desks, decorative houseplants, garden patios, comfortable living rooms, medieval brass lamps. This is scene-setting artwork, not experimental evidence or a shopping list.

stations.detail: Scene 01: molecular visualization and imaging laboratory. Wide view from the doorway towards an unoccupied microscopy station on the left: a credible modern upright fluorescence microscope with dark optical enclosure and camera module, small clean optical breadboard and neatly routed cables. To right, a dual-monitor workstation displays a magnified protein ribbon and ligand stick visualization plus a micrograph-style texture. In background, glass-front storage for slides and optical parts, a second lab bench and a real overhead service rail. Bright soft daylight mixed with neutral overhead light; subtle cool blue details. Frame as a medium-sized real university research room, not a luxury office.

Scene 02: molecular screening and assay automation laboratory. Diagonal perspective across an unoccupied light grey laboratory island: an enclosed automated pipetting workstation behind clear safety panels, microplate stacks, a compact plate reader with believable sliding tray, an equipment control monitor showing a grid of ranked molecular thumbnails and filter scatter plots. Deep background holds orderly racks and wall service outlets. Glazed partition to the side, muted pale green lab accents and neutral overhead panels. Main subject is the practical screening workstation and real precision instruments; not one ordinary laptop on a pretty table.

Scene 03: measurement-versus-prediction validation laboratory. View along a long pale epoxy bench from lower left into depth. A compact UV-visible spectrophotometer with sample compartment, a credible small analytical instrument stack with organized tubing inside a shallow service tray, calibration sample holder and precision balance on an anti-vibration slab. Two monitors beyond equipment show an actual-style measured-versus-predicted scatter plot and residual plot, without readable text. Through glass at back is another unoccupied measurement room. Neutral white illumination and restrained indigo instrument lights. Screen data is decorative scene content, no fabricated readable numerical results.

Scene 04: computational molecular discovery integration laboratory. Wide corner view with an L-shaped anti-static engineering bench, two compact compute towers with ventilated housings, a small glass-door equipment cabinet, an instrument interface module with tidy connected cables and status LEDs. Three mounted physical displays show linked computational workflow nodes, molecular structure panels and a diagnostic chart, no readable text. On the perpendicular bench is a compact benchtop analysis device, cable trunking and service rails connect the equipment. Exposed but orderly technical infrastructure, graphite and light grey finishes with restrained amber status LEDs, sophisticated genuine research integration environment.

Scene 05: target-research planning bay INSIDE an active structural biology facility, unoccupied. Camera beside a stainless service bench, looking past a physical tabletop ball-and-stick model and a slim workstation towards a large wall-mounted display showing a protein ribbon with a binding pocket. On the right a full-height glass partition reveals an actual analytical lab with instrument benches, overhead service rails, clean sample storage cabinets. Foreground has a closed research binder, precise technical printouts without legible text, stylus and a compact workstation. Clearly a laboratory planning bay, not a boardroom: no conference seating, no large wooden conference table, no luxury lounge, no art-gallery emptiness. Neutral daylight and pale slate laboratory finishes.

Scene 06: scientific data acquisition and sample-traceability laboratory. Strong depth perspective along a laboratory data station: small barcode scanner dock facing a neat microplate rack and unlabeled sample carriers, two real widescreen monitors showing data tables, molecular thumbnails and branching provenance graph with no readable text. Adjacent glass-enclosed equipment rack with organized network patch cords, a compact benchtop scanner and documented instrument connections. Frosted laboratory doors and glass-front catalog cabinets in background. White epoxy bench, brushed metal frames, neutral illumination and subtle cyan task lights, very realistic institutional research space. NOT a generic server farm; sample traceability and scientific instruments must be apparent.

Scene 07: molecular model evaluation and high-performance-computing laboratory. Eye-level wide view from the working position towards two technical control desks and a wall of four physical monitors, showing a prediction scatter plot, model comparison bars, tree structure and molecular views without readable text. At right behind a glass partition are just two realistic compact scientific GPU workstation cabinets with faint status indicators and neatly managed cables, at left a benchtop analytical instrument used for comparison. Grey antistatic surfaces, lab service rails, neutral overhead linear lights, soft teal screen accent. This should be a practical science lab for scrutinizing models, not a sci-fi spaceship or a cinema control room; believable scale.

Scene 08: candidate evidence review and reproducibility laboratory. View along a bright research handover bench, with two paired independent computer workstations showing the same molecular workflow and comparison charts from different views. A glass partition behind reveals a real analytical chemistry lab with an enclosed plate reader and a row of instrument modules; wall shelving holds orderly research binders and sample archives. Foreground laboratory bench has an open technical dossier with non-legible diagrams and a small molecule model on a stand. Pale grey epoxy and stainless steel, warm-neutral daylight and real ceiling laboratory lights, hopeful and confident without luxury decor. The point is scientific peer review inside a working laboratory, not a corporate meeting room.
